researched_by: the council's own motorhome guidance and individual car park pages, cross-read against the text of the 2023 Off Street Parking Places Order and the 2024 Amendment Order
policy_summary:
North Devon runs a real, published, priced overnight scheme and it has grown. Three council car parks take motorhomes overnight - North Walk in Barnstaple, Hillsborough in Ilfracombe and Bottom Meadow in Lynton - at GBP16 a night, two consecutive nights maximum, no return within 48 hours. The van must be self-contained with a BUILT-IN toilet, must not exceed 8m, and must be parked 6m clear of the next motorhome for fire safety. Payment is cash, card or the RingGo app; each car park is a separate RingGo zone.

Everything else is closed. The Off Street Parking Places Order carries a condition coded N10, 'No sleeping', attached to virtually every car park in the estate, and a separate condition H20, 'No overnight parking is permitted', on Barnstaple Bus Station and Albert Lane. So the district prohibits SLEEPING generally and PARKING specifically in a couple of places - a distinction that matters, because outside the three designated car parks the offence you commit by staying the night is sleeping, not parking. Enforcement is civil, by penalty charge notice, with contravention 91 (parked in an area not designated for that class of vehicle) the one aimed squarely at a motorhome in the wrong bay.

The trajectory is expansion. The 2023 Order had exactly one motorhome charge in the whole schedule, North Walk at GBP15. The 2024 Amendment Order added Hillsborough - both the car park and the lorry and van park - and Croyde, still at GBP15. The current position is three sites at GBP16, with Croyde dropped back to a daytime-only motorhome bay and Bottom Meadow in Lynton picked up instead. Small numbers throughout: Bottom Meadow has three motorhome bays, North Walk four oversized bays, Croyde one.

Note what is NOT covered. The Woolacombe beach car parks are not the council's - the Esplanade and Sandy Burrows are Parkin Estates, Marine Drive and Woolacombe Down are National Trust. Mortehoe car park IS council-owned, charges 8am-6pm and has no motorhome bay. On-street anywhere in the district, including the Saunton and Croyde approaches, is Devon County Council's, not North Devon's.
notes:
The most interesting thing here is the shape of the prohibition. Most authorities in this dataset restrict PARKING and let sleeping follow; North Devon does the reverse, writing 'No sleeping' into the ancillary conditions of the parking order itself and applying it estate-wide. That is a cleaner legal fit for the actual nuisance and it avoids needing a PSPO - the fifth or sixth authority confirming that the off-street parking order, not the PSPO, is the instrument of choice in England.

The self-containment test is stricter than most: a 'built in' toilet, not a portable one. Combined with the 8m length cap and the 6m spacing rule this is a scheme designed for a specific vehicle, and a large A-class or a converted van with a cassette in a cupboard may well fail it. The 6m spacing means the advertised bay counts overstate real capacity on a busy night.

Croyde is worth watching. It had a motorhome charge in the 2024 amendment and does not have one now; the current car park page carries 'No sleeping' and a single coach/motorhome bay charged to 6pm. Whether that was withdrawn on purpose or simply not carried into the 2025 consolidation is the one thing I could not settle - the 2025 Order PDF is the document that would say, and the council's server refused it.

Woolacombe, the pressure point named in the register, is largely outside the council's gift. The beach car parks are private and National Trust land. North Devon's provision sits at Barnstaple, Ilfracombe and Lynton - none of them where the surf crowd actually wants to be. That gap between where the bays are and where the demand is is the structural problem this scheme does not solve.

No camping or overnight-vehicle PSPO exists. The only live PSPO, extended to 2029 in 2026, covers boat-trip touting at Ilfracombe Harbour and has nothing to do with vehicles.
open_questions: The consolidated North Devon (Off Street Parking Places) Order 2025 - which revoked the 2024 Order and all its amendments - could not be retrieved; both published PDF URLs return 403. Its schedule is the authority for the current motorhome car park list and charges.
Was Croyde's motorhome charge deliberately withdrawn in the 2025 consolidation, or is the car park page simply out of date?
Does Hillsborough Lorry and Van Park still carry a motorhome charge separately from Hillsborough car park? The 2024 amendment listed both; the current guidance names only 'Hillsborough car park'.

Bay counts at North Walk and Hillsborough for motorhomes specifically. North Walk lists four 'oversized' bays and Hillsborough lists none separately; only Bottom Meadow publishes a motorhome bay count (3).
Whether the GBP16 overnight charge covers the 8am-6pm daytime tariff on the day of arrival or departure, or is additional to it.
Are there waste disposal or fresh water facilities at any of the three? None of the council pages mention an Elsan point. Bottom Meadow at least has public toilets on site.

sites.name: North Walk Car Park, Barnstaple
sites.notes: The original and longest-standing motorhome site - the only one in the whole 2023 Order, then at GBP15. Overnight subject to availability, vehicle not over 3,500kg and not over 8m, self-contained with a built-in toilet, parked 6m clear of the next motorhome. The wider car park has 62 standard bays and 4 oversized bays; the oversized bays are what a motorhome uses. Daytime tariff GBP1.40/hour or GBP14.00 for 10 hours, charged 8am to 6pm every day.
sites.geocode_precision: ONS centroid of EX31 1DU, the postcode the council publishes for the car park; the code was terminated in 2020 so the pin is the retired centroid, on North Walk by the River Taw

sites.name: Hillsborough Car Park, Ilfracombe
sites.notes: Added by the 2024 Amendment Order. 97 spaces in total with no separately published motorhome bay count - overnight is 'subject to availability', which in practice means whatever is free once you allow 6m between vans. All vehicles must park within the lines of a bay. Daytime tariff GBP0.70/hour up to 3 hours or GBP3.50 all day, charged 8am to 6pm. The adjacent Hillsborough Lorry and Van Park also carried a motorhome charge in the 2024 order; the current guidance names only this car park.
sites.geocode_precision: ONS centroid of EX34 9QJ, the postcode on the council's car park page, east of Ilfracombe harbour below Hillsborough hill fort

sites.name: Bottom Meadow Car Park, Lynton
facilities: public toilets on site (RADAR key for the accessible one)
sites.search_hint: Bottom Meadow car park, Castle Hill, Lynton
sites.notes: THE ONLY LYNTON AND LYNMOUTH SITE - the town council's own page is explicit that the motorhome bays are in Bottom Meadow ONLY. Three designated motorhome bays out of 143 spaces, the only site in the district that publishes a motorhome bay count. On-site public toilets. Chargeable 10am to 6pm, seven days, which is a later start than the coastal car parks. Sits below Lynton on Castle Hill, walkable to the cliff railway.
sites.geocode_precision: ONS centroid of EX35 6AR, the postcode both the town council and the tourism board give for Bottom Meadow on Castle Hill

sites.name: All other North Devon Council car parks
sites.notes: The Off Street Parking Places Order attaches ancillary condition N10, 'No sleeping', to virtually every car park in the estate. It is not a motorhome-specific rule - it bites on anyone sleeping in any vehicle - but it is what makes an overnight stay outside the three designated car parks a contravention. Enforced by penalty charge notice; contravention 91, 'parked in a car park or area not designated for that class of vehicle', is the one used against motorhomes in ordinary bays. Verified in the 2023 Order and carried through the 2024 Amendment Order; the 2025 consolidation could not be retrieved to confirm the wording is unchanged.

sites.name: Barnstaple Bus Station (Red Area) and Albert Lane (Blue Area), Barnstaple
sites.notes: The two places in the district where the Order goes beyond 'No sleeping' and prohibits the parking itself: ancillary condition H20, 'No overnight parking is permitted'. Leaving an empty vehicle overnight is a contravention here, which it is not in an ordinary council car park. Taken from the 2023 Order schedule.

sites.name: Croyde Car Park
sites.notes: A HOTSPOT WHERE PROVISION WAS WITHDRAWN. The 2024 Amendment Order gave Croyde a GBP15 motorhome charge; the current car park page carries 'No sleeping' and no overnight option. There is still one coach/motorhome bay out of 71 spaces, but it is a daytime bay - charged 8am to 6pm, GBP1.60/hour or GBP16.00 for 10 hours in summer. Lorries and coaches by appointment only. Whether the overnight charge was deliberately dropped in the 2025 consolidation or the page is stale is unresolved.
sites.geocode_precision: ONS centroid of EX33 1LX, the postcode on the council's car park page for Croyde village car park

sites.name: Mortehoe Car Park, Woolacombe
sites.notes: The council car park nearest the Woolacombe pressure point, and it has no motorhome provision at all - 89 bays, charged 8am to 6pm, no motorhome bay, covered by the estate-wide 'No sleeping' condition. Local tourism pages describe it as free overnight, which is true of the TARIFF but not of the sleeping condition; the charge stops at 6pm, the prohibition does not. Worth flagging to users because it is the obvious place an unbriefed van would head.
sites.geocode_precision: ONS centroid of EX34 7DT, the postcode on the council's car park page for Mortehoe village car park

sites.name: Woolacombe beach car parks (Esplanade, Sandy Burrows, Marine Drive, Woolacombe Down)
sites.notes: NOT COUNCIL LAND, and the single most common misunderstanding about Woolacombe. The Esplanade and Sandy Burrows car parks are Parkin Estates; Marine Drive and Woolacombe Down are National Trust. They close overnight, so North Devon Council's parking order does not reach them and the council's motorhome scheme cannot be extended to them. A 6m vehicle length cap applies at the Esplanade car park. Recorded here so the map does not imply council control of the beachfront.
